from_quote: No State shall enter into any treaty, alliance, or confederation; grant letters of marque and reprisal; coin money; emit bills of credit; make any thing but gold and silver a legal tender in payment of debts; pass any bill of attainder, ex-post-facto law, or law impairing the obligation of contracts; or grant any title of nobility
rationale: Quotes this clause in quotation marks as the first of the restrictions on the authority of the States.
to_quote: No State shall enter into any Treaty, Alliance, or Confederation; grant Letters of Marque and Reprisal; coin Money; emit Bills of Credit; make any Thing but gold and silver Coin a Tender in Payment of Debts; pass any Bill of Attainder, ex post facto Law, or Law impairing the Obligation of Contracts, or grant any Title of Nobility

from_quote: The right of coining money, which is here taken from the States
rationale: Continues the discussion of the clause quoted in the previous paragraph, taking up its words "coin money" as "the right of coining money, which is here taken from the States."

from_quote: The power to make any thing but gold and silver a tender in payment of debts, is withdrawn from the States
rationale: Continues the discussion of the clause quoted in the first paragraph, taking up in turn its prohibitions of "bills of credit," of a "tender in payment of debts," of "bills of attainder, ex-post-facto laws, and laws impairing the obligation of contracts," and of "titles of nobility."
to_quote: a Tender in Payment of Debts

from_quote: No State shall, without the consent of the Congress, lay any imposts or duties on imports or exports, except what may be absolutely necessary for executing its inspection laws, and the net produce of all duties and imposts laid by any State on imports or exports, shall be for the use of the treasury of the United States; and all such laws shall be subject to the revision and control of the Congress
rationale: Quotes this clause in quotation marks as the first part of the second of the restrictions on the States.
to_quote: No State shall, without the Consent of the Congress, lay any Imposts or Duties on Imports or Exports, except what may be absolutely necessary for executing it's inspection Laws: and the net Produce of all Duties and Imposts, laid by any State on Imports or Exports, shall be for the Use of the Treasury of the United States; and all such Laws shall be subject to the Revision and Controul of the Congress

from_quote: No State shall, without the consent of Congress, lay any duty on tonnage, keep troops or ships of war in time of peace, enter into any agreement or compact with another State, or with a foreign power, or engage in war unless actually invaded, or in such imminent danger as will not admit of delay
rationale: Quotes this clause in quotation marks as the second part of the second of the restrictions on the States.
to_quote: No State shall, without the Consent of Congress, lay any Duty of Tonnage, keep Troops, or Ships of War in time of Peace, enter into any Agreement or Compact with another State, or with a foreign Power, or engage in War, unless actually invaded, or in such imminent Danger as will not admit of delay

from_quote: power to make all laws which shall be necessary and proper for carrying into execution the foregoing powers, and all other powers vested by this Constitution in the government of the United States, or in any department or officer thereof
rationale: Quotes this clause in quotation marks as the first of the sixth class of powers.
to_quote: To make all Laws which shall be necessary and proper for carrying into Execution the foregoing Powers, and all other Powers vested by this Constitution in the Government of the United States, or in any Department or Officer thereof

from_quote: Had the convention attempted a positive enumeration of the powers necessary and proper for carrying their other powers into effect
rationale: Continues the discussion of the clause quoted in the previous paragraph, repeating its words "necessary and proper."

from_quote: Had they attempted to enumerate the particular powers or means not necessary or proper for carrying the general powers into execution
rationale: Continues the discussion of the clause quoted two paragraphs earlier, turning its words into "not necessary or proper," and refers to it as "this part of the Constitution."

from_quote: This Constitution and the laws of the United States which shall be made in pursuance thereof, and all treaties made, or which shall be made, under the authority of the United States, shall be the supreme law of the land, and the judges in every State shall be bound thereby, any thing in the constitution or laws of any State to the contrary notwithstanding
rationale: Quotes this clause in quotation marks as the second of the sixth class of powers.
to_quote: This Constitution, and the Laws of the United States which shall be made in Pursuance thereof; and all Treaties made, or which shall be made, under the Authority of the United States, shall be the supreme Law of the Land; and the Judges in every State shall be bound thereby, any Thing in the Constitution or Laws of any State to the Contrary notwithstanding

from_quote: The Senators and Representatives, and the members of the several State legislatures, and all executive and judicial officers, both of the United States and the several States, shall be bound by oath or affirmation to support this Constitution
rationale: Quotes this clause in quotation marks as the third of the sixth class of powers.
to_quote: The Senators and Representatives before mentioned, and the Members of the several State Legislatures, and all executive and judicial Officers, both of the United States and of the several States, shall be bound by Oath or Affirmation, to support this Constitution

from_quote: The election of the President and Senate will depend, in all cases, on the legislatures of the several States
rationale: Says the election of the President "will depend, in all cases, on the legislatures of the several States"; this clause has each State appoint electors "in such Manner as the Legislature thereof may direct."

from_quote: The election of the President and Senate will depend, in all cases, on the legislatures of the several States
rationale: Says the election of the Senate "will depend, in all cases, on the legislatures of the several States," the mode of choosing Senators set in this clause.
